A.explanation: P and Q are at the same distance $r$ from the point charge, so they are at the same electric potential and $W = q\Delta V = 0$.

B.explanation: This treats the radial separation $r$ as a potential difference, but P and Q have no change in $r$ so no work is done against the radial field.

C.explanation: This multiplies $E$ by the arc length $\pi r/2$, but movement along the arc is perpendicular to the radial field so no work is done.

D.explanation: This multiplies $E$ by a length $\pi r$, but force and displacement are perpendicular along the equipotential so the work is zero.

hints: Notice that P and Q are both exactly distance $r$ from the central $+$ charge, with a $90^\circ$ angle between them.
Connect equal radius to electric potential $V$ for a point charge: points at the same $r$ form one equipotential circle.
Connect work for a unit positive charge to potential difference using $W = q\Delta V$ with $q = 1$, and compare $V_P$ with $V_Q$.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: P and Q lie on the same circle of radius $r$ centred on the positive point charge, so $r_P = r_Q = r$.
State the rule: electric potential due to a point charge depends only on distance $r$, so all points on this circle have the same potential $V$.
State the work rule: work done per unit positive charge equals potential difference, $W = q\Delta V$ with $q = 1$, so $W = V_Q - V_P$.
Apply it here: since $V_Q = V_P$, then $\Delta V = 0$ and $W = 0$, even though the path length along the $90^\circ$ arc is $\pi r/2$.
The field does no work because any small displacement along the circle is perpendicular to the radial electric force. This is option A.
